text: Hmph. Another one, fresh off the road and staring up at the tower like it owes you something.
I'm Oswin. I keep the old stories here, and I don't hand them out to just anyone who wanders by. Ask carefully.
Well? What is it?

choices.label: Tell me about the four kings.
How do I keep my things between worlds?

text: You've been somewhere. I can smell another world's air on you.
One down doesn't make you clever. But it doesn't make you a fool either. Keep going.

choices.label: Tell me about the four kings.
How do I keep my things between worlds?

text: Four worlds. You actually did it.
The tower remembers what was lost. Take what you carry up to where the sky is closest, and see what it asks of you. Choose with care: a traveller walks only one road.
The tower in the sky. Built by people who knew far more than we do, and who are long gone.
Its four halls look out over four islands. Each island has a keeper who knows one world better than I ever will. Climb up, find them, listen to them.
Four kings, each guarding the way into a world of their own. They don't take kindly to intruders.
Which one do you want to hear about? And mind you, hearing about a king and beating one are not the same thing.
The guardian of the ocean is old, and he keeps his court in drowned halls beneath the waves, with his own kind around him.
Beyond him lies a world of endless water, where one last city still stands. The sea has never let anyone through while he keeps watch.
The Herald of the Sea knows more. Their island floats with drowned stone; you'll know it.
The dragon at the world's end keeps a world of endless sky and drifting isles.
Plenty have reached her. Fewer came back. The ones who did found that the way home was the way in.
The Herald of the Sky charts the clouds from the highest island. Ask them.
The three-headed undead destroys all who trespass in his eroded world, guarding the remains of his long-lost friends.
He hates the open sky, and anything that shines in it. Make of that what you will.
The Herald of the Sands keeps three black stones on a sun-baked island. They're kinder than I am.
The blind fool hunts in the deepest dark. Anger clouds his judgement; he knows no friend from foe.
His world is caves without end. The door, they say, remembers who was there at the end.
The Herald of the Deep keeps candles lit on the cave island. Speak quietly to them.
Most things you carry won't survive the crossing between worlds. Bound things will.
Rowan, our blacksmith, can bind an item to your soul. It stays with you when you travel and when you die. Your soul only holds so many, mind.
Each king that falls leaves something of its world with the one who felled it, and the soul can carry one more bound thing afterwards.
Long ago, mages and engineers worked side by side in one city. The mages held sky, sea, stone and flame by birth; the engineers learned to master them by craft.
Something broke that city. The Spire fell silent and the Foundry went cold. What waits at the end of either road, I don't know. Only that the old city may still stand.
The path of the mages leads to the Silent Spire. The path of the engineers leads to the Cold Foundry.
You walk only one. Don't ask me which. I'd only tell you the one I'd have picked, and I've been wrong before.
